keyframe_review.note: 297,167 km2 for 962-979: Ghazna and its hinterland (Ghazni, Kabul, Bamyan, Gardez; the shape covers all of Ghazni and Kabul provinces and 35% of Ghor). Page: 'Alp-Tegin established himself as the governor of Ghazna in 962' and in 977 Sabuktigin 'united the Turkic garrisons of Gardez, Ghazna and Bamyan'. keyframe_review.note: 705,183 km2 for 980-999. Page: 978 'Sabuktigin invaded Rukkhaj and Bust in the south of his realm', then Qusdar 'in north-east Baluchistan', and he 'captured the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar'; at his death in 997 he 'expanded his rule down to south of present-day Afghanistan and north of Balochistan'. keyframe_review.note: 2,994,472 km2, the largest shape. Page: 'On 26 May 1029, Mahmud entered Ray without resistance', Hamadan was captured and Isfahan 'seized in January 1030'; the Mas'ud I page adds that in 1030 the Kakuyid Muhammad 'wrested Ray from the Ghaznavids'. The shape holds Ray (72%), Hamadan (81%) and Isfahan from 1028, a year or two early, and keeps Ray to 1033. Review repair 2 (2026-10-24): the Kakuyid Muhammad took Ray in 1030 (ledger), and the Mas'ud I page implies the Ghaznavids had it back before the Kakuyid 'once again occupied Ray' in 1037/8 (governor of Jibal appointed 1033, invasion of western Iran 1035); the ledger regains Ray in 1033 (confidence 1). The shape therefore stands for 1033 only; 1028-1029 is the new keyframe ghaznavid-empire_1028b and 1030-1032 the new keyframe ghaznavid-empire_1030. No area figure on the page. Repair fx-01 (conflict with buyid-dynasty, 1,217 cells a year, Kerman 720 and Fars 497): Cliopatria's Ghaznavid shape from 1028 holds all of Fars and Kerman. The Buyid dynasty page lists Buyid rulers there ('Sultan al-Dawla (1012-1024)' and 'Abu Kalijar (1024-1048)' in Fars, 'Qawam al-Dawla (1012-1028)' in Kerman) and its only Ghaznavid act is that in 1029 Mahmud 'deposed Majd al-Dawla, replaced him with a Ghaznavid governor' at Ray; no page names a Ghaznavid hold on Fars or Kerman, so both are subtracted (the size rule had already given them to the Buyids).

keyframe_review.note: 105 km2 at 69.7-69.9 E, 28.3 N (Pakistan), a single cell. No page opened names any Ghaznavid land after 1186 (Lahore, 'the last Ghaznavid principality in Punjab'). The correction is the empty set.

correction.text: no territory: the Ghaznavid state ended in 1186

keyframe_review.note: The same 105 km2 cell as 1202-1205, for 1206-1209; Cliopatria's end year 1209 has no page behind it. The correction is the empty set.

region.text: Ghazna and its hinterland, taken by Alp Tigin in 962

ledger.note: 962: Alp-Tegin takes Ghazna from the local Lawik rulers. Page: 'Alp Tigin conquered the city from the local Lawik rulers in 962'; the Sabuktigin page: 'Alp-Tegin established himself as the governor of Ghazna in 962'. The Ghaznavids infobox dates the dynasty 977-1186 and the page says it was founded by Sabuktigin; this dossier follows Cliopatria in starting the state with the 962 seizure.

977: Sabuktigin, elected by the Turkic garrisons, founds the Ghaznavid dynasty proper. Page: Bilgetegin (966-975) and Boritigin (975-977) ruled before him and he held power 'until he was elected by them as their ruler in 977'. Same state and colour (rule 2).

region.text: Rukkhaj and Bust in the south of his realm

ledger.note: 978: Sabuktigin invades Rukkhaj and Bust in the south. Page: 'In 978, Sabuktigin invaded Rukkhaj and Bust in the south of his realm' and 'continued his expansion into Qusdar in north-east Baluchistan' (undated). The page does not say how the invasion ended; the gain is read from the 980 Cliopatria shape, which holds Bust.

region.text: the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar

ledger.note: 986: the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala marches on Ghazna. Page: Jayapala's 'march towards Ghazna with a large army in 986', a battle at Laghman and a snowstorm that 'devastated Jayapala's army'; the second march came in 988 'with an army composed of Afghans and Khalajs'.

region.text: the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar

ledger.note: 988: Sabuktigin wins the second battle of Laghman. After it he 'captured the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar'. The Mahmud page instead dates the annexation of Gandhara and Peshawar to 1001 (see there); the Cliopatria 980 shape already holds Peshawar.

region.text: the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar

ledger.note: 988: Sabuktigin takes the lands from Lamghan to Peshawar. Page: after the Second Battle of Laghman 'he captured the lands between Lamghan and Peshawar' (no month).

region.text: the eastern Khurasanian towns of Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat

ledger.note: 998: Mahmud, newly Sultan of Ghazna, is confirmed in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat. Page: 'That year, in 998, Mahmud then travelled to Balkh and paid homage to Amir Abu'l-Harith Mansur b. Nur II' and 'Mansur II confirmed Mahmud the possession of Ghazni, Bust, eastern Khurasanian towns of Balkh, Tirmidh, and Herat'. Mahmud's reign began March 998.

999: the Samanid lands of Khorasan pass to Mahmud, the Oxus becoming the border. Page: 'The Oxus River was decided as the borders between the two empires'; the Ghaznavids page: Mahmud 'completed the conquest of the Samanid and Shahi territories'. Page silent on the year; 999 is the end of Cliopatria's Samanid row and the Khorasan shape appears in 1000.

1001: Mahmud takes Peshawar and Gandhara from the Hindu Shahis. Page: 'On 28 November 1001, his army fought and defeated the army of' Raja Jayapala at the Battle of Peshawar; the page's timeline has Gandhara and Peshawar 'annexed after defeating Raja Jayapala'.

1001: the war with the Hindu Shahis moves east of Peshawar. Page: Peshawar 28 November 1001 and, on 31 December 1008, the defeat of the allied Hindu Shahi army at Chach; the zone is the Punjab between Peshawar and the Indus, which the page's 'annexed the region from Indus River to Nagarkot' makes the stake.
1002: Mahmud conquers Sistan. Page: 'In 1002, Mahmud invaded Sistan and dethroned Khalaf ibn Ahmad, ending the Saffarid dynasty.' The Cliopatria shape already holds Sistan from 1000.

1006: Mahmud marches on the Emirate of Multan. Page: 'In March-April 1006, left Ghazni and marched to Multan crossing near Peshawar'; 'in 1005 Mahmud [conquered Bhatia], and Multan in 1006'; the decisive expedition came in October 1010.

region.text: the region from the Indus River to Nagarkot

ledger.note: 1008: after Chach the Ghaznavids annex the Hindu Shahi land from the Indus to Nagarkot. Page: 'On 31 December 1008, Mahmud defeated the allied army of' the Hindu Shahi confederacy; 'After this victory Ghaznavids annexed the region from Indus River to Nagarkot'. The page's own timeline also has 'annexing only the Punjab region' in 1014 and 'Official annexation of Punjab' in 1021.
1008: the Hindu Shahi wars end at Chach (31 December 1008); the Punjab is annexed.
1010: Mahmud subdues Multan. Page: 'In October 1010, Mahmud launched a decisive expedition and successfully subdued Multan.' (The Ghaznavids page dates the Emirate of Multan to 1006.)
1010: the Multan war ends with the October expedition.

1011: Mahmud conquers Ghor. Ghurid page: the Ghurids 'gradually converted to Sunni Islam after the conquest of Ghor by the Ghaznavid ruler Mahmud of Ghazni in 1011', and its list of rulers has Muhammad ibn Suri ending in 1011 and Abu Ali ibn Muhammad ruling 1011-1035 'as vassals of the Ghaznavid Empire'. The Mahmud page has only 'In 1011, Sultan Mahmud led an expedition into eastern Ghur'; the region is the whole of Ghor on the Ghurid page's word, so confidence 2. Review repair 2 (2026-10-24): re-sourced from the Ghurid page (the first draft read the gain from the Cliopatria shape); the counterpart is the pre-Ghurid chiefs of Ghur, because the ghurid-dynasty dossier starts in 1152.
1017: Mahmud conquers Khwarazm. Page: 'In 1017 AD, Mahmud resolved to conquer Khwarazm which was under the Ma'munids'; he 'invaded Khwarazm, defeated the rebels on 3 July 1017, and captured Gurganj'.

1021: the Punjab is officially annexed. Page timeline: 'Official annexation of Punjab' in 1021, after 'annexing only the Punjab region' in 1014; Mahmud's failed attacks on Kashmir (1015 and once more) did not extend the border there.

1026: Sindh begins to pay tribute. Page: 'Sindh paid tribute from 1026 until his death in 1030 AD'; the page does not say Sindh was annexed. The page names no dynasty; the Sind-Habbari counterpart is read from Cliopatria's row for Sindh.
1029: Mahmud enters Ray. Page: 'On 26 May 1029, Mahmud entered Ray without resistance, seizing significant wealth'; Mas'ud I page: the Ghaznavids 'managed to annex the Buyid amirate of Ray'.
1030: the Kakuyids retake Ray. Mas'ud I page: 'in 1030 wrested Ray from the Ghaznavids' (it names Muhammad ibn Rustam Dushmanziyar). The page gives no month; Mahmud died on 30 April 1030.

1030: Hamadan and Isfahan fall to Mas'ud. Page: 'He first captured Hamadan and then advanced to Isfahan, which was seized in January 1030'; the page's timeline: 'Campaign in Persia led annexation Ray, Isfahan, Hamadan, Jibal from the Buyids and Kakuyids'.
1030: Sindh's tribute ends with Mahmud's death. Page: 'Sindh paid tribute from 1026 until his death in 1030 AD'; Mahmud died 30 April 1030.

1033: Ray is back under Ghaznavid governors. Page: Mas'ud 'appointed Abu Sahl Hamduwi as the governor of Jibal' (1033); 'In 1035, Mas'ud I launched another invasion of western Iran' and 'once again defeated the Kakuyid ruler Muhammad'; 'In 1037/8 ... Muhammad once again occupied Ray', which implies a Ghaznavid recovery after the 1030 loss. The page does not say when Ray itself was retaken: 1033 is the earliest year it supports and 1035 the latest, and the Cliopatria 1034 shape holds Ray. Review repair 2 (2026-10-24), confidence 1.

1034: Khwarazm breaks away under Harun. Page: Altun Tash 'was then succeeded by his son Harun' and 'In 1034, Harun declared independence from the Ghaznavids, and allied himself with the Kara-Khanid ruler Ali Tigin'.

region.text: Nasa, Farava and Dihistan in northern Khorasan

ledger.note: 1034: Mas'ud cedes Nasa, Farava and Dihistan to the Seljuks. Page: the Seljuks 'forced Mas'ud to cede Nasa, Farava and Dihistan' (the Dandanaqan page: 'Ma'sud gave the Seljuks three cities in Khurasan: Dihistan, Nasa, and Farawa'). The three lie on the north edge of Khorasan near Ashgabat; the radius is my approximation.

1035: the Seljuks, driven from Khwarazm, enter Khorasan. Page: 'Forced out of Transoxiana in 1034 by the Kara-Khanids, the Seljuks settled in Khwarazm' and 'His murder in 1035, forced them to flee through the Kara Kum Desert towards Merv'. The Mas'ud I page adds they 'began to gradually subdue the cities of Khorasan', took Nishapur and were expelled from Herat and Nishapur (undated).

1037: the Kakuyid Muhammad occupies Ray again. Page: 'In 1037/8, while Mas'ud was campaigning in India, Muhammad once again occupied Ray.' The page does not date the Ghaznavid recovery of Ray that 'once again' implies (it records Mas'ud's governor of Jibal in 1033 and an invasion of western Iran in 1035).
1040: the Seljuks win Khorasan at Dandanaqan. Page: the battle took place 'May 23, 1040' near Merv; 'Khorasan annexed by the Seljuks'; 'all of Khurasan fell to the Seljuk Turks'.

region.text: all the Ghaznavid lands in Persia and Central Asia: Khorasan, Jibal and the rest of the 1034-1039 shape beyond the 1040 shape

ledger.note: 1040: Dandanaqan costs the Ghaznavids Persia and Central Asia. Ghaznavids page: after the battle 'he lost all the Ghaznavid lands in Persia and Central Asia to the Seljuks', leaving 'modern-day Afghanistan, Pakistan and Northern India'; the Seljuks then 'captured Herat, Sistan, Pushang, Ghur' (undated). Mas'ud I page: 'Mas'ud thus permanently lost control of all of western Khorasan'.

1041-1050 (bridge): Mahipala of Delhi takes Hansi and Thanesar from Mawdud. Tomara Dynasty page: Mahipala 'probably imitated the same style after capturing Asigarh Fort in Hansi and Thaneshvara regions from Mawdud' (Mawdud of Ghazni, r. 1041-50); the page gives no year for the capture, so 1041, the start of Mawdud's reign, is the bridge year. Mirrors tomara-dynasty /ledger/1 (repair fx-01: the Ghaznavid side had no matching loss, and its shapes kept Haryana and Delhi to 1161).

1060: Ibrahim invades Ghur at the nobles' request. Page: 'In 1060, at the request of the nobles of Ghur, Ibrahim invaded the region.' The page does not state the outcome, and the Ghurid page (which does not mention Ibrahim) lists Muhammad ibn Abbas as ruling Ghor 1060-1080; the Seljuks 'captured Herat, Sistan, Pushang, Ghur' after Dandanaqan (Dandanaqan page), so a Ghaznavid return to Ghor is the page's implication and the gain is a bridging judgment (confidence 1). Review repair 2 (2026-10-24): counterpart changed from ghurid-dynasty (whose dossier starts in 1152) to the pre-Ghurid chiefs of Ghur.

1148: the Ghurids beat Bahram-Shah at Ghazni. Page: 'By 1148, Sayf al-Din Suri returned with an army, scored a victory at the Battle of Ghazni while Bahram fled to Kurram'; Bahram 'marched back to Ghazna' (undated; the Ghaznavids page: retaken 'the next year').

1152: the Ghurid attempt on Ghazna ends with Ala al-Din Husayn's defeat. Page: Husayn, after the sack of Ghazni (1150/1151, 'the city burned for seven days and seven nights'), 'In 1152 ... refused to pay tribute to the Seljuks' and was 'defeated and captured at Nab in the Harirud Valley by Sultan Ahmed Sanjar'; Ghazna stayed Ghaznavid until 1161/2.

1161 (latest year the pages allow): Ala al-Din Husayn of Ghor takes Zamindawar, Bust and Bamiyan. Ghurid page: he 'managed to conquer Garchistan, Tukharistan, Zamindawar, Bust, Bamiyan and other parts of Khurasan' after his release from Sanjar (captured 1152, a prisoner for two years); the Ala al-Din Husayn page: he 'died in 1161'. Neither page dates the conquests or says they were Ghaznavid land (the Bahram-Shah page has Bahram marching 'from Zamin-Dawar' and fleeing to the fortress of 'Bamian'), so the loss is a bridging judgment between the Cliopatria shape, which holds them to 1176, and the 1162 keyframe. The ghurid-dynasty dossier (sa-04) carries no matching gain.

By 1161 (no page gives the year): Multan has passed from the Ghaznavids to the Qarmatians. Ghurid page: in 1175 Muhammad of Ghor 'captured Multan from the Carmathians', so the Ghaznavids no longer held it; the Emirate of Multan page has the 1041 Ismaili revolt end with the khutba read for Mawdud and gives no later date. The loss lies between 1041 and 1175; 1161 is the last year before the 1162 keyframe, which omits Multan. The same counterpart string is used in the ghurid-dynasty dossier (1175 gain).

1162: the Oghuz Turks seize Ghazni; the Ghaznavids retreat to Lahore. Page: 'In 1161/2, a group of Oghuz Turks seized the Ghaznavid capital of Ghazni, forcing Khusrau Malik to retreat to Lahore, which became his new capital.' The Ghaznavids infobox gives Ghazni 977-1163. Ghurid page: 'In 1173, Muhammad of Ghor ... reconquered the city of Ghazni from the Ghuzz Turks'. Review repair 2 (2026-10-24): this event covers Ghazni and Zabulistan only (the Ghaznavids page: 'Ghazni and Zabulistan were lost to a group of Oghuz Turks'); the rest of the lost land has its own events (1161 and 1162, below).
1162: the capital moves from Ghazna to Lahore. Page: the retreat to Lahore, 'which became his new capital'.

region.text: the rest of the Afghan and Baluchi lands of the 1152 shape: Kandahar, Nimroz, Paktika, Uruzgan, Kabul valley, Nangarhar and Pakistani Baluchistan (about 700,000 km2)

ledger.counterpart: Ghuzz Turks, Ghurids and local rulers (pages silent)
ledger.note: 1162: with Ghazni gone the Ghaznavids keep Lahore and the Punjab. The Khusrau Malik page gives them only Lahore, the Punjab and incursions 'as far as southern Kashmir' and names none of Kabul, Kandahar, Bust, Sistan or Baluchistan; the Ghaznavids page says only that 'Ghazni and Zabulistan were lost'. No page opened says who took the rest of the 1152 shape or when, so it is dropped at 1162 with the retreat to Lahore (confidence 1), as the 1162 keyframe requires. Review repair 2 (2026-10-24).

region.text: the southern part of Ghaznavid Punjab

ledger.note: 1178: Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad of Ghor invades Ghaznavid Punjab. Page: 'In 1178 the Ghurid ruler Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad invaded the southern part of Ghaznavid Punjab'.
1179: the Ghurids seize Peshawar. Page: 'In 1179/80 he seized Peshawar'; in 1181/2 Muhammad 'swept around Lahore, but Khusrau Malik managed to keep him from the city by paying him'.

region.text: the southern part of Ghaznavid Punjab

ledger.note: 1186: the Punjab war ends with the fall of Lahore. Ghurid page: they 'annexed the last Ghaznavid principality in Punjab, with their capital in Lahore, in 1186 through stratagem'.

region.text: Lahore and the Punjab, the last Ghaznavid principality

ledger.note: 1186: Muhammad of Ghor takes Lahore and ends the Ghaznavids. Ghurid page: 'annexed the last Ghaznavid principality in Punjab, with their capital in Lahore, in 1186 through stratagem'; Khusrau Malik page: 'Lahore was finally captured by the Ghurids in 1186', Khusrau Malik and his sons were taken to Ghur and executed in 1191 or 1192 ('No member from the house of Ghazni was allowed to survive'). Cliopatria keeps specks to 1209.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Hindu Shahi wars

zones.text: the Punjab from Peshawar to Nagarkot

wars.outcome: Ghaznavid victory: Sabuktigin took the lands from Lamghan to Peshawar (988), Mahmud won at Peshawar on 28 November 1001 and at Chach on 31 December 1008 and annexed the region from the Indus to Nagarkot.
wars.note: Sabuktigin page for 986 and 988; the Mahmud page dates the annexation of Gandhara and Peshawar to 1001, the Punjab to 1014 or 1021.

wars.name: Ghaznavid intervention in the Samanid civil war
wars.outcome: Sabuktigin and Mahmud fought for the Samanid emir against the rebels Fa'iq and Abu Ali (Khorasan taken 23 October 994, Nishapur lost and retaken 995); in 998 Mansur II confirmed Mahmud in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat and the Oxus became the border.
wars.note: The page does not say how the Samanids lost the rest of Khorasan; see the 999 ledger event (confidence 1).

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Sistan
wars.outcome: Mahmud dethroned Khalaf ibn Ahmad and ended the Saffarid dynasty.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Multan
wars.outcome: Mahmud marched on Multan in March-April 1006 and 'successfully subdued' it in October 1010.
wars.note: Bhatiya fell in 1005 on the page.

wars.name: Ghaznavid invasion of Kashmir
wars.outcome: 'In 1015, Mahmud unsuccessfully attacked Kashmir'; after two failed attempts he did not try again. No border moved.
wars.note: The year of the second attempt is not on the page.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Mahmud beat the rebels on 3 July 1017 and captured Gurganj; Khwarazm broke away again under Harun in 1034.

wars.name: Ghaznavid expedition to Kannauj and Mathura
wars.outcome: Mahmud took the seven forts of Kannauj (arrived 20 December 1018) and plundered Mathura; the cities were sacked, not annexed.

wars.name: Ghaznavid campaign in Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Mahmud invaded Transoxiana in September 1024; Qadir Khan allied with him at Samarkand on 29 April 1025 and Mahmud 'left Samarkand to Qadir Khan'. No border moved.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of the Jibal
wars.outcome: Mahmud entered Ray on 26 May 1029; Mas'ud took Hamadan and Isfahan (January 1030); Ray was lost to the Kakuyids in 1030.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Kakuyid struggle for Ray
wars.outcome: Kakuyids wrested Ray in 1030; Mas'ud named a governor of Jibal in 1033 (Ray back under Ghaznavid governors by then, ledger confidence 1) and invaded western Iran in 1035; Muhammad 'once again occupied Ray' in 1037/8.

wars.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory near Merv on 23 May 1040; Khorasan annexed by the Seljuks, the Ghaznavids restricted to Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Seljuk clash at Sakalkand
wars.outcome: Ibrahim sent an army into Sakalkand in January 1073 after about fourteen years of peace; the Seljuks drove it out. No border moved.

wars.name: Sanjar's campaign against Bahram-Shah
wars.outcome: After Bahram stopped paying tribute, Sanjar marched on Ghazna in 1135 and Bahram fled to Lahore; he remained a Seljuk tributary.

wars.name: Ghurid-Ghaznavid war for Ghazni
wars.outcome: Sayf al-Din Suri beat Bahram at Ghazni in 1148; Bahram retook it; Ala al-Din Husayn sacked it (1150/1151) and was beaten and captured by Sanjar at Nab in 1152.

wars.name: Oghuz seizure of Ghazni
wars.outcome: Oghuz Turks seized Ghazni in 1161/2 and Khusrau Malik retreated to Lahore; the Ghurids reconquered it from the Ghuzz in 1173.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of the Ghaznavid Punjab
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor invaded in 1178, took Peshawar in 1179/80, was bought off at Lahore in 1181/2 and captured Lahore in 1186, ending the dynasty.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened; the Oxus border of 999-1017 follows a river, the Seljuk frontier after 1040 is undefined, and the Punjab limits are approximate.

notes:
Pages: nine opened (the Ghaznavids, Mahmud, Dandanaqan, Sabuktigin, Ghurid dynasty, Khusrau Malik, Mas'ud I, Ibrahim, Bahram-Shah); budget 9. Failed titles: Bahram-Shah_of_Ghazni, Bahram-Shah, Bahram_Shah_of_Ghazni; Bahram-Shah_of_Ghazna loaded.
Start: the Ghaznavids page's infobox dates the state 977-1186 (Sabuktigin); Cliopatria starts at 962 (Alp-Tegin); this dossier follows Cliopatria and records 977 as a rename event.
Cliopatria faults (all in keyframe_review): 1000 and 1015 shapes include Khwarazm 17 years early; 1028 shape includes Ray, Hamadan and Isfahan a year or two early and keeps Ray to 1033 (page: lost 1030); all shapes 1040-1176 carry 782 Iranian cells (Sistan and Baluchestan, Kerman, Hormozgan) that the page excludes; 1152 shape holds Ghazni fifteen years after the Oghuz took it (1161/2); 1177 shape holds Multan, taken by the Ghurids from the Carmathians in 1175; the 1188, 1202 and 1206 shapes are specks of 284, 105 and 105 km2 after the dynasty's end in 1186 and are marked wrong.
Pages disagree: the Mas'ud I infobox gives his death as 17 January 1040, but the Dandanaqan page puts the battle on 23 May 1040 and the sultan's flight after it; the Ghaznavids page says Ghazni fell in 1163 and also 'around 1170'; Khusrau Malik says Ghazni fell to the Oghuz in 1161/2 and the Ghurid page that the Ghurids took it from the Ghuzz in 1173; the Mahmud page dates the Punjab's annexation to 1001, 1008, 1014 and 1021; Bahram-Shah's death is c. 1152 (infobox) or 1157 (text).
Seljuk suzerainty: Bahram-Shah was installed in 1117 as a Seljuk vassal and paid tribute for his whole reign (Bahram page); Ibrahim had made peace with Malik-Shah. This belongs in the Great Seljuk dossier as vassal_start 1117 / vassal_end c. 1152, counterpart ghaznavid-empire (me-09).
Counterparts: ma-munid-dynasty (Khwarazm) and lawik-dynasty, which have no dossier; hindu-shahis, kakuyids and emirate-of-multan have one (written by other groups); Harun of Khwarazm (short-lived breakaway governor, no dossier proposed), and the Shansabani chiefs of Ghur before 1152.
Not dated by the pages opened: when the Ghaznavids took Ghur outright; whether Makran and Kerman were held (Mahmud page entry cut off; Mas'ud I page: Kerman 'conquered' but the inhabitants preferred Buyid rule); the fate of Isfahan and Hamadan after 1030; Herat and Sistan after Dandanaqan; the Ghaznavid-Qarmatian Multan; Ibrahim's 1079 Pakpattan fortress (too small to map).
Cross-checks with sibling dossiers already on the mount (read by grep, not edited): hindu-shahis has the Laghman rout in 991 (this dossier: 988 from the Sabuktigin page), Peshawar 28 Nov 1001, Chach 31 Dec 1008, peace 1009, Nandana 1014 and 'Annexed by the Ghaznavids: 1026' for the end of the Shahis; emirate-of-multan agrees on 1006 and 1010; sind-habbari-dynasty has Mansura invaded 1025 and 'conquered by the Ghaznavids in 1026' where the Mahmud page here has Sindh paying tribute 1026-1030; buyid-dynasty has Ray taken in March/April 1029 where the Mahmud page has 26 May 1029; oghuz-turks has Shah Malik taking Khwarezm from the Ghaznavids in 1041 after Harun's 1034 independence; qarmatians and oghuz-turks name this state as successor or counterpart.
